acceptance: A hosted `@slow` or `@plan` oracle review through the gateway completes, with its longest silent stretch measured from the gateway log, or a reproducible failure is recorded with its cause.
If silent stretches past the idle limit fail, the gateway or reviewer setting is changed and the fix verified the same way.
context:
2026-10-28 close-out (owner decision: close on the @plan evidence; reopen if a timeout ever appears): 29 CI reviewer captures since run 40606584392, every review exited 0, none timed out. Two @plan reviews of PR 3571 went through the gateway (21 and 14 requests matching 21 and 14 turns in ~/.omp/oracle-gateway/home/.omp/logs). Longest silence about 53 s (run 40609022552: 53.4 s between request starts, 52.7 s longest single request); longest request in any tier 57.7 s; time to first output at most 7.6 s. Limits: gateway idle timeout 255 s (18.12.1 and 18.13.2), client stream timeouts 300 s, reviewer kill at 30/40/45 min, job 255 min. Caveats: the gateway log records request starts only (silence inside a request is bounded, not measured); no @slow review ran in the window; the pi-native format has no gateway keepalive, so a single provider silence over 255 s could still hit the idle limit.

description: Once PR #3296 moves the reviewer onto the scoped auth-gateway, every reviewer request streams through `omp auth-gateway serve` on the owner's Mac. The local test of that setup did not include a request with a long silent stretch. The gateway runs on Bun, whose server idle timeout is at most 255 seconds; the gateway's setting and its keepalive behaviour during provider silence were not checked. A high-effort `@slow` or `@plan` review can think longer than that before emitting output, so long reviews could fail as absent. Start after #3296 merges.
